paper.title: Conversational Dueling Bandits in Generalized Linear Models

settings.name_in_paper: Conversational dueling bandits with generalized linear model (GLM)
unmapped: Conversational mechanism: besides arm-pair duels, the learner can query pairwise comparisons of key-terms (feature = weighted average of related arm features via known bipartite weight matrix W) at frequency b(t) = b*t, b in (0,1); key-term queries incur no regret
The learner knows the arm/key-term weight matrix W and the key-term features
Regret is average utility regret of the dueled pair: u(a*) - (u(a)+u(a'))/2
Key-term set assumed to span R^d each round
settings.definition_quote: At round $t$, given the candidate arm set $\mathcal{A}_t$, we present to the user a pair of arms $(a_t, a_t^{\prime}) \in \mathcal{A}_t\times \mathcal{A}_t$ and ask for his/her relative preference. ... $o_t$ follows the Bernoulli distribution $Ber(\mu(d_t^T\theta_*))$

unmapped: MNL choice feedback over an assortment of size at most q (q = m) with a no-purchase option; reward is expected revenue of the assortment
Conversational key-term queries (subsets of key-terms with MNL feedback) at frequency b(t) = b*t
The learner knows kappa_2 (MNL curvature constant), the revenues r_{j,t}, and the key-term weight matrix
settings.definition_quote: We also define $\mathcal{C}$ to be the set of candidate assortments with size less than $q$ ... The user purchase decision $o_t\in C_t\bigcup \{0\}$ is observed ... The cumulative expected regret over time $T$ is defined as: $R(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T (R_t(C_t^*,\theta_*) - R_t(C_t,\theta_*))$.

symbols.t_0: burn-in time 4(C_1 sqrt(d)+C_2 sqrt(log(1/delta)))^2/(b lambda_B^2) from Lemma 2
symbols.b_conv: conversation frequency constant, b(t)=b*t, b in (0,1)
symbols.lambda_B: minimum eigenvalue of E[(x-y)(x-y)^T] for x,y sampled from the key-term barycentric spanner

conditions: mu twice differentiable with bounded derivatives (Assumption 2)
conversation frequency b(t) = b*t with b in (0,1)
tuning: key-term pairs sampled independently from barycentric spanner

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: With probability (1-$\delta$), our algorithm has the following regret upper bound: R(T)\leq t_0+\frac{32}{\kappa_1}(R\sqrt{d\log((1+\frac{4\kappa_1(T+ b T)}{d\lambda})/\sigma)}+\sqrt{\lambda\kappa_1}\|\theta_{*}\|_2)\sqrt{\frac{T}{2b\lambda_B}} = \mathcal{O}(\frac{1}{\kappa_1}\sqrt{d T\log(T)})

results.notes: Paper writes /sigma inside log, apparently a typo for delta; recorded as delta. kappa_1 mapped to c_mu, R to sigma, ||theta_*|| to S (<=1). Regret is realized sum of utility gaps of the pair, bounded w.p. 1-delta. Horizon: algorithm does not appear to require T.

conditions: conversation frequency b(t) = b*t with b in (0,1)
results.notes: Asymptotic form of Theorem 1; hides dependence on b, lambda_B and delta.

conditions: conversation frequency b(t) = b*t, b in (0,1)
assortment size at most q (m = q)
tuning: alpha_t = (1/(2 kappa_2)) sqrt(2 d log(1+(b(t)+t)/d) + 2 log t)
T_0 = O(max{(1/kappa_2^2)(d log((b(T)+T)/d) + 4 log T), q/sigma^2, 256/(b q lambda'_B) log(128 d/(delta lambda'_B^2))})

source.label: th2
source.quote: Assume conversation frequency to be $b(t) = b \cdot t$, with $b\in(0,1)$, and $\alpha_t = \frac{1}{2\kappa_2}\sqrt{2d\log(1+\frac{b(t) + t}{d})+ 2\log(t)}$, and $T_0 = \mathcal{O}(...)$. The expected regret of ConMNL is upper bound by $R_T = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{dTq\log(T)}).$

results.notes: q (assortment size) mapped to m. Regret defined via expected revenues, so pseudo_regret. Setting mapping (dueling feedback with subset comparison, combinatorial) is approximate for MNL choice feedback. T_0 depends on T, so horizon known.
